body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: 51b7a8d3171b91496ae0834149a42426a05c79ee -->

Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.

What looks good:
- The default-cap pin moved to its own binary, `import_step_guard_default_cap`. Its assertions are unchanged.
- The two capped pins in `import_step_guard` no longer use a 30 s wall-clock limit. They use a 120 s hang barrier. The evaluation cap is still the real bound. This is the option issue #1605 allowed: a raised limit plus one generous outer barrier.
- The test count holds. Main has 6 tests in `import_step_guard`. The head has 5 there and 1 in the new binary. No test was removed or weakened.
- The new binary's header carries its Gate map, as the test-file law requires.
- Only test files and one decision file changed. No product code changed.
- The cause analysis matches the fix. Cargo runs test binaries one after another. The cheap pins no longer queue behind the 50 s import in the same process.

Results, merged with main 1bd9298d6, on the self-hosted runner (macOS): https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/43587748270
- Quick gate: 1 step, 0 failed, 57 s wall. It ran both binaries: `import_step_guard` (5 tests) and `import_step_guard_default_cap` (1 test).
- Clippy with `-D warnings` on camcraft-app, all targets: clean.

Requested before merge: none.

Questions / notes (not blocking):
1. The two test files arrive with CRLF line endings. Only 2 of the 1988 Rust files on main have CR bytes; the old file had LF. The rewrite shows every line as changed. Convert the two files to LF in a follow-up, so later diffs stay small.
2. Issue #1605 asks for a mutation check named in the PR. The body does not name it. The lowered-cap pin asserts the guard's message "within 100000 evaluations". Without the guard that assert fails, or the import hangs and the 120 s barrier trips. Add that one line to the body or the decision file.
3. The batch tier now runs a ~52 s debug binary on every pass. The existing entries in `xtask/src/plan.rs` SLOW_BINARIES are the same size, and batch skips them. The decision file says the pin must stay in the batch gate. Revisit if batch time grows.
4. The moved doc comment in the new binary says "the lowered-cap pins below". The pins are now in the other binary.

Not exercised: the heavy binary did not run beside two other gates on this runner. The author's 30 parallel runs, with the heavy binary active, cover that case. The runner checked its own OS only; these tests carry no per-OS values.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
